THE FULL COMPARISON

Overall performance.

Astra ranks second overall. OpenWAM-α leads the benchmark. Inspect the scores and task-level differences across all eight systems.

THE EXPERIMENT

A different route
to robot control.

EBench tests household, retail, and industrial manipulation. Here, a general-purpose multimodal model selects robot actions from images, measured state, and a compact task demonstration.

01 / ASTRA

Context-driven action selection

RGB observations and robot state inform end-effector, gripper, and base commands. The model observes execution and chooses its next action.

02 / VLA & WAM BASELINES

Learned robot policies

The 26 benchmark tasks are represented in VLA/WAM training. Astra receives one historical demonstration per task, with no task-specific parameter updates. No learned policy generates or refines Astra’s action requests.

26 tasks · 510 episodes

19 mobile and 7 tabletop tasks across nine scene categories.

Seen tasks · one-demo ICL

A fixed package of 10–18 annotated keyframes is reused across instances of each task.

Unseen composition · zero-shot

Two constituent tasks are combined into one ordered procedure, without an Astra demonstration.

EXECUTION LIMITS / PRECISION & HORIZON

Progress is not
completion.

Reaching an object or repairing a local mistake is only part of the task. Precise contact and reliable completion remain difficult.

DISCUSSION

From task understanding
to reliable execution.

The evaluation places general-purpose agentic control alongside seven learned robot policies. Astra ranks second overall, with a stronger profile on mobile manipulation than on tabletop tasks. The videos expose both observation-conditioned revision and unresolved precision and completion requirements.

In-context learning and unseen task composition are distinct settings in this study. The case studies make their procedures visible; the full technical report will develop the implications for embodied research.
